title: Goods 18 - Weights and Dimensions of Goods Vehicles
source: RSA, Guidelines on Maximum Weights and Dimensions of Mechanically Propelled Vehicles and Trailers (April 2015 edition, published by the IRHA in 2019)

questions.q: What is the maximum height of any vehicle in Ireland, including its load?
questions.exp:
All vehicles: 4.65 m, and the load is included. The only exception is a vehicle carrying baled agricultural produce (hay, silage, straw).
📍 RSA weights and dimensions guide, maximum height

questions.q: What is the maximum width of a rigid truck, tractor unit or semi-trailer with a design gross vehicle weight over 3.5 tonnes?
questions.exp:
Rigid trucks, tractor units, trailers and semi-trailers over 3.5 t: 2.55 m. A vehicle of 3.5 t or less: 2.5 m. A conditioned (insulated, temperature-controlled) vehicle: 2.6 m.
📍 RSA weights and dimensions guide, maximum width

questions.q: A temperature-controlled 'conditioned' vehicle has insulated side walls at least 45 mm thick. What is its maximum width?
questions.exp:
A conditioned vehicle, built to carry goods at controlled temperatures with side walls (insulation included) at least 45 mm thick, may be 2.6 m wide. Other heavy goods vehicles: 2.55 m.
📍 RSA weights and dimensions guide, definitions and maximum width

questions.q: What is the maximum overall width of a vehicle together with its load (other than loose agricultural produce)?
questions.exp:
Vehicle plus load: 2.9 m (9 feet 6 inches). The load itself may not stick out more than 300 mm beyond either side of the vehicle.
📍 RSA weights and dimensions guide, maximum load overhang

questions.q: How far may a load project beyond either side of a goods vehicle or trailer?
questions.exp:
Side overhang: no more than 300 mm (1 foot) on either side, and the vehicle with its load must stay within 2.9 m wide.
📍 RSA weights and dimensions guide, maximum load overhang

questions.q: How far may a load project beyond the rearmost point of a vehicle or trailer?
questions.exp:
Rear projection: no more than 3 m (electricity and telephone poles are an exception). If the load sticks out more than 1 m, a warning device must be carried at the rear of the load in daytime.
📍 RSA weights and dimensions guide, maximum load overhang

questions.q: A load projects 1.5 m beyond the rear of a trailer in daytime. What is required?
options: A warning device on the load
questions.exp:
Above 1 m of rear overhang a warning device must be carried at the rear of the load during the day. The absolute limit is 3 m.
📍 RSA weights and dimensions guide, maximum load overhang

questions.q: What is the maximum length of a rigid truck?
questions.exp:
Rigid truck: 12 m. A trailer is also 12 m. (13.5 m and 15 m are the limits for buses.)
📍 RSA weights and dimensions guide, maximum length

questions.q: What is the maximum length of an articulated vehicle (tractor unit and semi-trailer)?
questions.exp:
Articulated vehicle: 16.5 m. Vehicles first registered before 1 January 1991 and not over 15.5 m are not affected. A rigid truck with a drawbar trailer may be 18.75 m.
📍 RSA weights and dimensions guide, maximum length

questions.q: What is the maximum length of a rigid truck towing a drawbar trailer (road train)?
questions.exp:
A combination of a rigid vehicle and a drawbar trailer: 18.75 m. The maximum loading space of a truck and trailer combination is 16.40 m.
📍 RSA weights and dimensions guide, maximum length and loading space

questions.q: On a semi-trailer, the 12.0 m length limit is measured from:
options: The front bumper to the rear
The kingpin to the rear of the trailer
The first axle to the last axle
The landing legs to the rear doors
questions.exp:
For a semi-trailer, 12.0 m is measured from the axis of the kingpin to the rear of the trailer. The swing radius (kingpin to any point on the front of the trailer) may not exceed 2.04 m.
📍 RSA weights and dimensions guide, maximum length

questions.q: Every vehicle and combination must be able to turn within the area between two circles. What are their radii?
questions.exp:
Turning circle: the vehicle or combination must be driven between concentric circles of 12.50 m and 5.30 m radius without any part going outside that area.
📍 RSA weights and dimensions guide, manoeuvrability criteria

questions.q: What is the maximum weight on a single non-driving axle?
questions.exp:
Single axle: 10 t. The sole driving axle may carry 10.5 t, or 11.5 t with air suspension or an equivalent system.
📍 RSA weights and dimensions guide, axles and wheels

questions.q: What is the maximum weight on the sole driving axle of a lorry with air suspension?
questions.exp:
Sole driving axle with twin tyres: 10.5 t, or 11.5 t with air suspension or an equivalent system.
📍 RSA weights and dimensions guide, axles and wheels

questions.q: What is the maximum weight on a triaxle whose outer axles are 1.3 m or more apart?
questions.exp:
Triaxle: 24 t if the spacing is 1.3 m or more, 21 t if less. A tandem with 1.3 m or more spacing: 18 t.
📍 RSA weights and dimensions guide, triaxle and tandem axles

questions.q: What is the maximum laden weight of a two-axle rigid truck whose axles are 3 m or more apart?
questions.exp:
Two-axle rigid: 18 t with an axle spacing of 3 m or more, 16 t if less than 3 m.
📍 RSA weights and dimensions guide, rigid vehicles

questions.q: What is the maximum laden weight of a three-axle rigid truck with twin tyres and air suspension on the driving axles?
questions.exp:
Three-axle rigid: 25 t, or 26 t with twin tyres and air suspension (or equivalent) on each driving axle. The tonnes-per-metre rule (5.5 t per metre of wheelbase) also applies.
📍 RSA weights and dimensions guide, rigid vehicles

questions.q: What is the maximum laden weight of a four-axle rigid truck that is an 'appropriate motor vehicle'?
questions.exp:
Four-axle rigid: 30 t, or 32 t if it is an appropriate motor vehicle (twin tyres, air suspension on driving axles, ABS). The Department kept it at 32 t to protect roads and bridges.
📍 RSA weights and dimensions guide, rigid vehicles

questions.q: An 'appropriate motor vehicle' (needed for the higher weight limits) must have:
options: 3+ axles, twin tyres, air suspension, ABS
A Euro 6 engine and a smart tachograph
A refrigerated body and side guards
questions.exp:
Appropriate motor vehicle: at least three axles, twin tyres, air suspension (or equivalent) on each driving axle and ABS brakes, with the required plate.
📍 RSA weights and dimensions guide, definitions

questions.q: What is the maximum weight of a five-axle articulated vehicle made of a 2-axle tractor unit and a 3-axle semi-trailer?
questions.exp:
2+3 articulated: 40 t. Ireland allowed 42 t under a derogation until 30 June 2016; that has ended. A 3-axle 'appropriate' tractor with a 2-axle semi-trailer (3+2) may run at 42 t.
📍 RSA weights and dimensions guide, two-axle tractor unit combinations

questions.q: A 3-axle 'appropriate' tractor unit pulls a 2-axle semi-trailer carrying a 40-foot ISO container on an intermodal journey. What is the maximum weight?
questions.exp:
3+2 appropriate combination: 42 t, rising to 44 t when carrying a 40-foot ISO container on an intermodal journey.
📍 RSA weights and dimensions guide, three-axle tractor unit combinations

questions.q: What is the maximum weight of a six-axle articulated vehicle (3+3) that meets all the extra safety criteria?
questions.exp:
Since 1 April 2013 a 3-axle tractor with a 3-axle semi-trailer may run at 46 t if both are 'appropriate' and meet the extra criteria (EBS; ESC on tractors and roll stability control on trailers registered from that date). Otherwise 44 t.
📍 RSA weights and dimensions guide, note 6

questions.q: To run at 46 tonnes, a tractor unit and semi-trailer already in service on 1 April 2013 need:
options: EBS braking (ABS alone is not enough)
ABS braking on every axle only
A speed limiter set at 80 km/h
A second driver on every trip
questions.exp:
Vehicles already in service need EBS (ABS is not sufficient). New tractor units also need Electronic Stability Control and new semi-trailers roll stability control.
📍 RSA weights and dimensions guide, note 6

questions.q: Since when may six-axle rigid truck and drawbar trailer combinations run at 46 tonnes?
questions.exp:
From 1 June 2015 six (or more) axle rigid truck and drawbar trailer combinations may run at 46 t, with EBS and, for new vehicles, ESC and roll stability control. Artics got 46 t on 1 April 2013.
📍 RSA weights and dimensions guide, note 7

questions.q: A four-axle tractor unit with a semi-trailer would weigh more than 46 tonnes. What is needed?
options: Nothing if the tyres are new
questions.exp:
A four-axle tractor unit with an appropriate semi-trailer follows the manufacturer's specification, but over 46 t it needs a local authority permit (abnormal load).
📍 RSA weights and dimensions guide, four-axle tractor units

questions.q: The 'tonnes per metre' rule for most articulated combinations allows how much weight per metre of distance from the kingpin to the rearmost axle?
questions.exp:
Most articulated combinations: 5.5 t per metre (from the kingpin to the centre of the rearmost axle). For a 46 t six-axle combination it is 5.75 t per metre.
📍 RSA weights and dimensions guide; S.I. No. 43 of 2013
